name: Chromium
occurrence: Mined mainly as chromite ore; named from the Greek 'chroma' (colour) for its vividly coloured compounds.
majorUses: Chrome plating for corrosion-resistant shiny finishes
safetyNotes: Hexavalent chromium (Cr⁶⁺) compounds are toxic and carcinogenic, unlike the much safer trivalent Cr³⁺ form your body actually needs in trace amounts.
notableCharacteristics: Its electron configuration breaks the expected filling order — one electron jumps from 4s to 3d to give a more stable half-filled 3d⁵ set, a classic exception every chemistry student memorizes.
whyHere: A half-filled 3d⁵ subshell is unusually stable, so chromium 'steals' an electron from 4s to achieve it — the textbook exception to the normal electron-filling order.
didYouKnow: Chrome plating isn't solid chromium — it's a microscopically thin layer over another metal, thin enough that the underlying metal's shape and weight barely change.
genZNote: Broke the electron-filling rules just to be more stable. Also the reason your bike handlebars are shiny.
